newsitem.title: USA: Home builders Lennar, Pacific Greystone in merger.
newsitem.headline: Home builders Lennar, Pacific Greystone in merger.

text.p: Lennar Corp., said Wednesday it will spin off its commercial real estate business and acquire rival home builder Pacific Greystone Corp., creating the nation's fifth largest home builder and a leader in the Sun Belt market.
Lennar, a closely held home builder based in Miami, said it will hold 68 percent of the merged company.
Each share of Pacific Greystone will be exchanged for 1.138 shares in the new company. With 14.96 million shares outstanding, the transaction values Pacific Greystone at about $514 million.
Stock in Pacific Greystone, which was based in Los Angeles, was down $1.75 at $15.375 and Lennar was up $3.875 at $30.25, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts estimated the commercial real estate unit being spun off will be worth $18 and $24 per share. Lennar expects to spin off the new company, which will be called LPC Inc., in the fourth quarter. The division finances, owns, develops and manages commercial real estate.
Lennar shareholders will receive one share of LPC for each share of Lennar held on the distribution date.
The new Lennar Corp. will be comprised of the existing home building and residential financial services operations of both Lennar and Pacific Greystone.
The combined companies will have operations in Florida, California, Texas, Arizona and Nevada.
Lennar is controlled by its founder and chairman, Leonard Miller, who, through ownership of a Class B series of stock, holds 79 percent of the voting shares.
